title: CHASM: Cross-frequency Harmonized Axis-Separable Mixing for Spectral Token Operators
claim: Unlike independent per-frequency channel mixers, sharing one learned channel basis across frequencies with frequency-specific gains yields a structured, drop-in separable mixer block.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; contrast, operator math, then block flowchart; dashed dividers
description: Three side-by-side panels separated by dashed lines, each with a blue underlined title. Panel (a) shows a conventional approach. An H×W×C feature cube goes through an rFFT. Four frequency rows k1 to k4 follow. Each row maps a channel vector through its own coloured matrix W(k) to an output vector. A bracket labels these independent per-frequency mixers, and a red box notes there is little cross-frequency structure. Panel (b) opens with an orange formula box, M(k)=U diag(λ_k) Uᵀ with λ>0. Below it a chain runs Uᵀ, diag(λ), U, with shared and frequency-specific labels. A gain table of orange cells and a small U matrix follow, with the note that the same U is shared across all frequencies. Panel (c) is a vertical flowchart. Input feeds CH-plane mixing (blue) and CW-plane mixing (orange), then local refinement (green) and a 1×1 fusion projection (yellow). A residual sum gives the output. Side annotations explain the axis-separable design.
caption: Overview of CHASM. (a) Standard spectral mixers often learn independent channel operators for different Fourier bins, with little explicit cross-frequency structure. (b) CHASM introduces cross-frequency harmonization by sharing a learned channel eigenbasis \(U\) across frequencies while retaining frequency-specific positive gains \(\lambda_k\). (c) The resulting operator is applied separably along the height--channel and width--channel planes, followed by local refinement and \(1\times1\) fusion, yielding a drop-in replacement mixer block.
abstract: Spectral token mixers based on Fourier transforms provide an efficient way to model global interactions in visual feature maps. Existing designs often either apply filter-wise spectral responses along fixed channel axes, or learn adaptive frequency-indexed channel mixing without explicitly aligning the channel directions used across frequencies. We propose CHASM, a Cross-frequency Harmonized Axis-Separable Mixer, as a structured middle ground. CHASM separates what should be shared from what should remain frequency-specific: all frequencies share a learned channel eigenbasis, while each frequency retains its own positive spectral gains. The shared basis makes channel directions comparable across the spectrum, whereas the positive gains preserve local spectral adaptivity. CHASM applies this structured operator separably along the height and width axes and is used as a drop-in replacement mixer inside existing backbones. We provide a structural characterization of the shared-basis operator family and evaluate CHASM through controlled same-backbone comparisons. Across accelerated MRI reconstruction, undersampled MRI segmentation, and natural-image reconstruction, CHASM consistently improves over same-backbone spectral-mixer baselines. Ablations show that removing the shared-basis constraint weakens performance, and randomizing coherent sampling geometry substantially reduces the gain, supporting cross-frequency harmonization as a useful inductive bias for spectral token operators.
